cards.title: Act Like You Belong
cards.instruction: You do not understand what is happening. Copy the confidence around you and never admit confusion.

cards.title: Make the Choice Rewrite the Past
cards.instruction: Make them choose between options whose consequences reinterpret an earlier promise, refusal, or agreement.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've signed the shop lease where you signed. Choose the overseas job or this shop; you said we'd build something together.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I signed as a witness. You've put your name in the witness box too.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course, witnessed intentions. Which of us is signing as the actual partner?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I could take the job and send money for the shop. You'd run it here.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then send the first month's rent. We'll call 'together' your money and my days behind the counter.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 copies witness signing as business commitment and tests a shared promise; A3 masks role confusion; A5 makes B4 remote-money offer the concrete meaning of together.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 witness correction prompts A3 actual-partner choice; B4 funding/labor division causes A5 first-rent request and reinterpretation.

relationship.evidence: B4 offers a feasible compromise rather than merely refusing A's binary.

heightening.evidence: A5 accepts B4 new option but requires money now to make the earlier promise mean financial rather than daily partnership.

specificity.evidence: A1 lease/job/shop, B2 witness box and A5 first rent make the proposed division materially specific.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 rent request replaces vague signing status and the remaining sentence tells B what accepting means.
